scenario: [LNUL.4.10]: a `null` operand does not absorb a fault. With `n` null and `z` zero, `s.n + s.a // s.z` and `s.a // s.z + s.n` are each the DIVIDE_BY_ZERO the floor-division raises, not [LNUL.4.1]'s `null`, on either side of `+`. Two rules, one per side, so a runtime that let a null LEFT operand skip the right one records one error, not two. Path: the non-connective BINOP arm — libds rete/eval.c (both operands evaluated, the fault forwarded before the null test), Mercury ds.eval.m eval_node(e_binop(...)) (the else branch of `connective`).
rules_ds:
schema S scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    n: Int? mutable
    a: Int mutable
    z: Int mutable

rule null_left:
    S s where s.n + s.a // s.z > 0
->
    log info "left"

rule null_right:
    S s where s.a // s.z + s.n > 0
->
    log info "right"
